page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m4.large is an entry-level virtual server instance belonging to the ecs.e family. It is configured with 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on a KVM hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned at the lower end of the compute spectrum. Multi-core and single-core CPU tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds of approximately 2.01 GB/sec and 1.99 GB/sec respectively. Redis SET operations achieve 1.35 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is limited to 0.26 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation and modest resource density make this instance suitable for budget-conscious scenarios where continuous high-performance compute is not required. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU architecture, which can lead to variable performance under noisy-neighbor conditions, alongside the lack of baseline network bandwidth and bundled local storage.

This instance is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, development and testing environments, low-traffic database operations, and simple background tasks that do not require sustained high CPU utilization or high-speed network throughput.
